title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 156
paragraphs: Having given this charge upon the road, Cyrus continued his march to the native land of the Persians; but Pactyas, hearing that an army was approaching to fight against him, was struck with fear and at once fled to Kyme. Then Mazares the Mede marched upon Sardis with a certain portion of the army of Cyrus, and as he no longer found Pactyas or his followers at Sardis, he first compelled the Lydians to perform the commands of Cyrus. By his commands the Lydians changed the whole manner of their life. After this, Mazares sent messengers to Kyme bidding them give up Pactyas. The men of Kyme resolved to refer the question to the god at Branchidai, asking what counsel they should follow. For there was there an Oracle established of old, which all the Ionians and Aiolians were accustomed to consult, and this place lies in the territory of Miletos above the port of Panormos.
